title: Erdős Problem #1166: Most-Visited Points in Planar Random Walk
description: Is the union of most-visited sites in a planar random walk bounded by a polylogarithmic function almost surely?

overview.historicalContext:
Erdős Problem #1166, posed by Erdős and Révész, concerns the geometry of planar random walks. Given a random walk in Z², let F(k) be the set of most-visited points after k steps. The question asks whether the total number of distinct most-visited points up to step n grows at most polylogarithmically.

The answer is YES: almost surely |⋃_{k ≤ n} F(k)| ≪ (log n)². Key ingredients include the Erdős-Révész result that |F(n)| ≤ 3 a.s. for large n, and the Erdős-Taylor theorem on maximum visit counts.

This problem is catalogued at erdosproblems.com/1166.
